diagnosis: Customer is receiving HTTP 429 responses and believes the Retry-After header is not being respected by their client. Enterprise account with premium support; no indication of a platform-side issue. The correct backoff procedure is described in kb-0014.
reply:
Hello,

When you receive a 429 Too Many Requests response, the `Retry-After` header indicates the number of seconds your client should wait before making the next attempt. Our clients should honour that value and also add a random jitter to spread retries evenly. If you see sustained 429s across a full rate-limit window, that may point towards the plan's throughput ceiling rather than a temporary burst.

I am referencing our guide "Reading 429 responses and backing off correctly" (kb-0014) which covers this in more detail. Please let us know if adjusting your retry logic still leaves you hitting the limit.
